correctness.rationale: The five-cycle Fourier eigenvalues yield the degree-unrestricted sharp q bound eta. A nonnegative real cosine polynomial of degree ≤3 vanishing at the interior chord has a double root, so P(x)=(x-c)^2(A+Bx). The third-harmonic coefficient B/4 must be nonnegative by Bochner positivity, hence its linear factor is nondecreasing and q≤eta²; equality forces B=0, giving the unique normalized quadratic. Exact quartic factorization with residual quadratic discriminant 1−sqrt(5)<0 establishes global pointwise nonnegativity of the explicitly nonnegative-Fourier degree-four optimizer. A clique-based copositivity proof for H=J−2A and exact negative trace show non-CP; a degree-four nonnegative Fourier perturbation has disjoint zeros, supplies all five Fourier residues and maintains strict Horn separation for 0<delta<9−4sqrt(5). Exact symbolic identities have been replayed with verify.py; no finite tests substitute for the universal proof.

originality.rationale: The matrix-level pentagon DNN/CP separation is known (Burer–Anstreicher–Dür 2009 and Peyré 2026), and is expressly credited. The identifiable new mathematical assertion is the sharp pointwise-nonnegative positive-definite Fourier interpolation inequality at pentagonal chord zeros: every degree-at-most-three admissible polynomial satisfies q≤(3−sqrt(5))/2 with a unique degree-two extremizer, whereas degree four achieves the PSD upper bound (sqrt(5)−1)/2; a degree-four perturbation retains a non-CP strictly positive/full-rank five-point Gram. The inspected classical primary matrix text, entire 2026 pentagon exposition, and recent positive-definite interpolation work do not prove this joint degree-constrained statement. This assessment is best-knowledge and not an independent historical-priority certificate.

value.rationale: The C5 sparsity graph is the canonical five-dimensional gap between doubly nonnegative and completely positive Gram matrices, so the opposite-chord zero constraint is intrinsic rather than arbitrarily chosen. The theorem determines a precise minimal Fourier degree for a globally pointwise-nonnegative, positive-definite circle interpolation of that natural matrix, with a nontrivial golden-ratio gap below the threshold and unique cubic-class optimizer. The same bandwidth admits a strictly positive polynomial and full-rank non-CP Gram, showing robustness under smoothing without a broader theorem claim. The classical matrix obstruction alone does not answer this interpolation invariant.
